shots.title: How instant coffee is made
shots.sub: Real coffee, brewed in a factory, with the water taken back out
shots.vo: Instant coffee is real coffee, brewed in a factory, with the water taken back out. Here is how it is made.

shots.title: 1 · Roasting
shots.sub: Green beans tumble in a drum at 215 °C for about 12 minutes: they lose 17 % of their weight and turn brown
shots.vo: Green beans tumble in a drum at over 200 degrees for about twelve minutes. They lose a fifth of their weight and turn brown.

shots.title: 2 · Grinding
shots.sub: Corrugated rollers crack the beans into a coarse 1 mm grind, so water can flow through it
shots.vo: Corrugated rollers crack the roasted beans into a coarse, even grind, so water can flow through it.

shots.title: 3 · Extraction
shots.sub: Water at 180 °C under pressure dissolves 40 % of the grounds: a strong, dark liquor at 20 % solids
shots.vo: In tall steel columns, water at up to 180 degrees and high pressure dissolves about forty percent of the grounds. What comes out is a strong, dark liquor.

shots.title: 4 · Clarification
shots.sub: A disc centrifuge spins out the fine sediment and leaves the liquor clear
shots.vo: A centrifuge spins the liquor and throws out the fine sediment, leaving it clear.

shots.title: 5 · Concentration
shots.sub: Under vacuum the liquor boils at only 50 °C: more than half of the water leaves without cooking the flavour
shots.vo: Under vacuum, the liquor boils at only fifty degrees. More than half of the water leaves without cooking the flavour. Now it is a thick coffee syrup.

shots.title: 5A · Spray drying (the powder route)
shots.sub: The syrup is sprayed into air at 250 °C: each droplet dries in a fraction of a second
shots.vo: The cheaper route: the syrup is sprayed into air at 250 degrees. Each droplet dries in a fraction of a second into a fine powder.

shots.title: 5B · Agglomeration
shots.sub: A mist of steam sticks the powder into porous clumps that dissolve easily
shots.vo: A mist of steam sticks the powder into porous clumps that dissolve easily.

shots.title: 6 · Freezing
shots.sub: The syrup is poured on a belt and runs through a tunnel at −45 °C: it comes out as a solid frozen slab
shots.vo: The syrup is poured on a belt and runs through a tunnel at minus forty-five degrees. It comes out as a solid frozen slab.

shots.title: 7 · Granulating
shots.sub: The slab is broken into 1–3 mm frozen granules
shots.vo: The slab is broken into small frozen granules, sized for how fast they should dissolve.

shots.title: 8 · Freeze drying
shots.sub: At 0.5 mbar the ice turns straight into vapour without melting, and freezes again on a cold condenser
shots.vo: In a vacuum chamber the trays are gently warmed. At half a millibar the ice does not melt: it turns straight into vapour, which freezes again on a cold condenser. The granules dry without ever getting hot.

shots.title: 9 · Packing
shots.sub: A puff of nitrogen pushes the oxygen out of the jar before the seal, so the coffee stays fresh for years
shots.vo: The dry granules go into jars. A puff of nitrogen pushes out the oxygen before the seal, so the coffee stays fresh for years.

shots.title: 120 g of green coffee → 41 g of instant · about 21 cups
shots.sub: Nothing added: brewed coffee with the water taken out, frozen and dried
shots.vo: Nothing added. Brewed coffee with the water taken out, frozen and dried. Back to coffee in a stir.
